_provisional: Authored in Rebel-Sim per FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §0. As of M3, this is checked against the real Rebel-ROM reference implementation (a sibling checkout, not in this repo) rather than invented from the spec docs alone: sysvar GROUP NAMES, ORDER, and OFFSETS below match src/sysvars.h and src/screenmodule.h exactly. One deliberate divergence: Rebel-ROM packs sysvar fields as byte/u16 C structs; Rebel-Sim stores every field as a full 4-byte cell for uniformity with the rest of this engine, so FIELD offsets within each group do NOT match Rebel-ROM byte-for-byte, only the group-level map does. Primitive token IDs and the DICT/RSTK/CHAR bank contents are Rebel-Sim-only (Rebel-ROM's Forth/Phase 11 doesn't exist yet) and have no real counterpart to reconcile against.
_dovarDoconDodoesNote: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §7: three more reserved Code Field sentinel values, same tier as docolTokenId (checked once at the START of executeXT, never iterated over in the slot-processing loop the way primitive token IDs are). Negative so they're visually and numerically distinct from both DOCOL (0) and the positive 1..N primitive token space, and from -1 (inner.ts's own TOP_LEVEL_SENTINEL, a return-stack VALUE, not a code-field value, so no real collision risk either way).

primitives.note: formats the popped number in the current BASE and streams it (plus a trailing space) through screen.emit(), one character at a time

primitives.name: EMIT
primitives.note: pops a raw character code and streams it through screen.emit() (M3: a real CHAR-bank + framebuffer write, matching Rebel-ROM's CScreenModule::Emit — \r/\n are handled as control codes there, not glyphs)

primitives.name: CR
primitives.note: M3: screen.emit(10) — Rebel-ROM's Emit() special-cases '\n' as cursor-to-next-row rather than treating CR as a HAL call of its own

primitives.name: EXIT
primitives.note: pops the return stack into IP; only meaningful inside a compiled word body, special-cased by the inner interpreter (M2)

primitives.name: LIT
primitives.note: pushes the next parameter-field cell as a data literal and skips over it; only meaningful inside a compiled word body, special-cased by the inner interpreter (M2)

primitives.name: CHAR!
primitives.note: ( col row code -- ) M3: CScreenModule::WriteChar's 3-arg default-ink/paper overload — writes the CHAR bank cell and blits the glyph via the injected ScreenHal

primitives.name: CHAR@
primitives.note: ( col row -- code ) M3: CScreenModule::ReadChar — reads the CHAR bank directly, no framebuffer involved; out-of-range returns 32 (space), matching Rebel-ROM

primitives.name: CLS
primitives.note: ( -- ) M3: CScreenModule::Cls — fills the CHAR bank with spaces, clears the framebuffer to the current PAPER color, resets the cursor to 0,0

primitives.name: AT-XY
primitives.note: ( col row -- ) M3: CScreenModule::SetCursor — sets CURSOR-X/CURSOR-Y directly, no bounds-checking (matching Rebel-ROM; an out-of-range cursor self-corrects on the next EMIT via AdvanceCursor's wrap)

primitives.name: INK
primitives.note: ( color -- ) M3: sets the SCREEN group's default foreground color sysvar used by CHAR!/EMIT/. when no override is given. Rebel-Sim stores this as a raw 24-bit 0xRRGGBB truecolor value (Rebel-ROM's TColor is likewise a raw pixel value, not a palette index — direct/truecolor mode is its likely default per docs/SCREEN-MODULE.md §4)

primitives.name: PAPER
primitives.note: ( color -- ) M3: same as INK but for the background color

primitives.name: KEY?
primitives.note: ( -- flag ) M4: CKeyboardModule::ReadEvent peeked non-destructively — TRUE if the event queue is non-empty, matching FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md's hal_key_pressed? non-blocking-read requirement

primitives.name: KEY
primitives.note: ( -- char ) M7: blocks (FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §7a) — suspends the running session via inner.ts's generator-based step loop until the bound Channel (channel.ts, default KeyboardChannel) has a translated-char event, then pops and pushes it. M4's original throw-on-empty behavior is gone; KEY?/token 29 is unchanged (still a raw, unfiltered, non-blocking peek at the Keyboard queue).

primitives.name: ACCEPT
primitives.note: ( addr len -- len2 ) M7a: classic Forth line-input. Reads chars one at a time off the bound Channel (blocking, like KEY), echoing each via screen.emit() and storing into the arena at addr; Backspace (char 8) erases the last echoed char (wraps back across a screen row boundary if needed) without going below the start of this call's input; Enter (char 10) terminates without being stored. Fully special-cased in inner.ts's dispatch — never reaches primitives.ts's switch, since it needs many blocking points (one per character), not just one.
( addr -- x ) M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §4: cell fetch. addr must be cell-aligned — no defined behavior for misaligned reads, matching the cell model.
( x addr -- ) cell store, same alignment requirement.

primitives.name: C@
primitives.note: ( addr -- x ) byte fetch, zero-extended, no alignment requirement.

primitives.name: C!
primitives.note: ( x addr -- ) byte store (low 8 bits of x).
( n addr -- ) add n to the cell at addr. STANDARD-for-now per §3 (DUP @ ROT + SWAP ! once LOAD exists) but shipped as a primitive today, same reasoning as everything in §9.

primitives.name: >R
primitives.note: ( x -- ) ( R: -- x ) M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §5: move top of data stack to return stack. Unbalanced against R>/EXIT corrupts the return address — a real, documented footgun this spec doesn't guard against, not an oversight.

primitives.name: R>
primitives.note: ( -- x ) ( R: x -- ) move top of return stack to data stack.

primitives.name: R@
primitives.note: ( -- x ) ( R: x -- x ) copy top of return stack without removing it.

primitives.name: BRANCH
primitives.note: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §6: unconditional jump — reads the next cell as a target ip value and jumps there. Only meaningful inside a compiled word body; special-cased by the inner interpreter exactly like LIT/EXIT (M2), not a primitives.ts case. Never dictionary-called directly.

primitives.name: 0BRANCH
primitives.note: conditional jump — pops a flag; FALSE behaves like BRANCH, TRUE skips the target cell and continues. Same inner-interpreter special-casing as BRANCH.

primitives.name: IF
primitives.note: ( flag -- ) IMMEDIATE, compile-time only: compiles 0BRANCH + a placeholder cell, pushes the placeholder's address (for ELSE/THEN to patch) onto the data stack — safe since IMMEDIATE words run even while compiling (same DOCOL-note mechanism ':'/';' already use).

primitives.name: ELSE
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: compiles BRANCH + a placeholder (jumps past the else-branch); patches IF's placeholder to just past this cell; pushes its own placeholder address.

primitives.name: THEN
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: patches the address on top of the stack (from IF or ELSE) to point at HERE.

primitives.name: BEGIN
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: pushes HERE (a backward-branch target) — emits nothing.

primitives.name: UNTIL
primitives.note: ( flag -- ) IMMEDIATE: compiles 0BRANCH + BEGIN's address (known immediately, backward, no patching needed).

primitives.name: WHILE
primitives.note: ( flag -- ) IMMEDIATE: compiles 0BRANCH + a placeholder (forward exit target), leaving BEGIN's address underneath on the stack for REPEAT.

primitives.name: REPEAT
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: compiles BRANCH + BEGIN's address (backward); patches WHILE's placeholder to HERE.

primitives.name: RECURSE
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: compiles a direct call to the *current*, still-HIDDEN definition's own cfa — computed straight from LATEST, bypassing findWord's HIDDEN skip (the same skip that made M2 leave this unsupported). Resolves M2's documented cut.

primitives.name: DO
primitives.note: ( limit index -- ) IMMEDIATE: compiles a call to (DO), pushes HERE as the loop-back target. DO never pre-checks limit vs. index — classic Forth behavior, not a bug: LOOP is what tests, and only after the body has already run once, so `limit index DO ... LOOP` with limit=index still runs one iteration before terminating.

primitives.name: LOOP
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: compiles a call to (LOOP), then 0BRANCH back to DO's target (popped from the data stack).

primitives.name: +LOOP
primitives.note: ( n -- ) IMMEDIATE: as LOOP, but compiles a call to (+LOOP) instead — increments by a value popped from the data stack at runtime rather than by 1.

primitives.name: (DO)
primitives.note: Runtime helper LOOP-family words compile calls to — not meant to be typed directly (parenthesized, classic-Forth convention for 'internal'). Pops limit then index off the data stack, pushes them onto RSTK above the current return address (docs §5's >R/R> warning applies to this pairing too).

primitives.name: (LOOP)
primitives.note: Runtime helper: increments RSTK's loop index by 1, compares to the limit; pushes FALSE (continue — LOOP's compiled 0BRANCH will jump back) or TRUE (done) onto the data stack; on done, also drops the loop-control cells off RSTK.

primitives.name: (+LOOP)
primitives.note: Runtime helper: as (LOOP), but pops the increment off the data stack instead of using 1.

primitives.name: I
primitives.note: ( -- n ) pushes the innermost DO loop's current index (peeks RSTK depth 0, doesn't pop).

primitives.name: J
primitives.note: ( -- n ) pushes the next-innermost DO loop's index (peeks RSTK depth 2 — past the innermost loop's own index+limit).

primitives.name: (DOES>)
primitives.note: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §7: what DOES> compiles a call to. Only meaningful inside a compiled word body; special-cased by the inner interpreter (needs the live ip register and performs an EXIT-like return-stack unwind), never dictionary-called directly. At runtime: rewrites LATEST's own Code Field to dodoesTokenId, stores the current ip (which — since this dispatch already advanced past its own slot — is exactly the address of the code following DOES> in the *defining* word) into LATEST's leading parameter-field cell (the does-pointer DODOES reads), then ip = rstack.pop() (unwinds back to whatever called the defining word).

primitives.name: HERE
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) current dictionary-growth pointer — already tracked internally since M2, just not callable from Forth until now.

primitives.name: LATEST
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) address of the most recently defined dictionary entry — same situation as HERE. Needed by any dictionary-walking word (WORDS, §12).
( x -- ) compiles x as the next cell at HERE, advancing HERE — the same primitive compileCell() (dictionary.ts) already does internally, now exposed to Forth source.

primitives.name: ALLOT
primitives.note: ( n -- ) advances HERE by n bytes without writing anything — reserves raw space.

primitives.name: VARIABLE
primitives.note: ( "name" -- ) NOT immediate (matches real ANS Forth) — at runtime, consumes the next word directly from whatever input is currently being interpreted (Machine.nextInputToken(), the same shared cursor ':' uses — works correctly even when VARIABLE is itself called from deep inside another word's execution, not just typed directly), creates a dovarTokenId-coded entry, and compiles *two* cells: a leading does-pointer slot every dovarTokenId word reserves (same as CREATE, inert until/unless DOES> is ever applied) initialized to 0, then the variable's actual storage, also initialized to 0. Executing the new word pushes the second cell's address — dovarTokenId's dispatch always skips the reserved leading cell, for both VARIABLE- and CREATE-made words.

primitives.name: CONSTANT
primitives.note: ( x "name" -- ) pops x, consumes the next input word as the name (same mechanism as VARIABLE), creates a doconTokenId-coded entry storing x in its one parameter cell. Executing the new word pushes x — the value, not an address, which is the whole reason doconTokenId exists as a separate sentinel from dovarTokenId.

primitives.name: CREATE
primitives.note: ( "name" -- ) consumes the next input word as the name (same mechanism as VARIABLE), creates a dovarTokenId-coded entry and compiles one leading cell (initialized to 0) — the does-pointer slot DODOES reads *if* DOES> is later applied to this word; permanently unused otherwise, the one fixed cost of not knowing in advance whether DOES> is coming. Executing the new word (before any DOES>) pushes the address *past* that reserved cell — wherever HERE happens to be right after CREATE returns, exactly where a following `,`/ALLOT starts writing.

primitives.name: DOES>
primitives.note: IMMEDIATE: compiles a single call to (DOES>). Everything else about the CREATE...DOES> mechanism lives in (DOES>)'s own runtime behavior and dodoesTokenId's dispatch, not here.

primitives.name: (SLIT)
primitives.note: M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §8: string-literal runtime helper, generalizing LIT's inline-literal mechanism (FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §5) to a byte run instead of one cell. Only meaningful inside a compiled word body; special-cased by the inner interpreter: reads the next cell as a byte length, pushes (ip, length) as the string's addr/len, then advances ip past the string bytes rounded up to the next cell boundary (alignCell) — never dictionary-called directly.

primitives.name: S"
primitives.note: ( "string" -- addr len ) IMMEDIATE, dual-mode (DEVELOPING.md §7, M16): while compiling, compiles (SLIT) + the string's byte length + the raw string bytes inline, same as before; while interpreting, copies the text into the PAD bank and pushes its addr/len directly — real interpret-time behavior, not a throw. Multi-word strings work in both modes (DEVELOPING.md §2.4). PAD text longer than PAD's size throws rather than corrupting adjacent arena memory.

primitives.name: TYPE
primitives.note: ( addr len -- ) prints len characters starting at addr through screen.emit(), looped.

( "string" -- ) IMMEDIATE, dual-mode (DEVELOPING.md §7, M16): while compiling, sugar for S" ... TYPE, unchanged; while interpreting, emits the text directly through screen.emit() with no PAD involvement (nothing needs to persist past the print).

primitives.name: 2DUP
primitives.note: ( a b -- a b a b ) M8, CORE-VOCABULARY.md §9: STANDARD-for-now, shipped as a primitive since there's no loader yet (§3).

primitives.name: -ROT
primitives.note: ( a b c -- c a b )

primitives.name: TUCK
primitives.note: ( a b -- b a b )

primitives.name: NIP
primitives.note: ( a b -- b )

primitives.name: ?DUP
primitives.note: ( x -- x x ) if x is nonzero, ( x -- x ) otherwise.

primitives.name: DEPTH
primitives.note: ( -- n ) current data stack depth.

primitives.name: /MOD
primitives.note: ( a b -- rem quot )

primitives.name: MIN
primitives.note: ( a b -- min )

primitives.name: MAX
primitives.note: ( a b -- max )
( n -- n/2 ) arithmetic shift right by 1.
( a b -- flag ) M1 shipped = but not its negation.
( n -- flag )
( n -- flag )

primitives.name: U<
primitives.note: ( a b -- flag ) unsigned comparison.

DEVELOPING.md §2: comment. ( -- ) IMMEDIATE, not compile-only — while compiling, consumes input up to the matching ')' and retains it as compiled (SLIT)+2DROP inline data (a genuine no-op at runtime, Jupiter-Ace style, not discarded like classic Forth); while interpreting at the top level, consumes and discards it since there's no HERE to compile into.

DEVELOPING.md §6 (system vocabulary loading): tick. ( -- xt ) Not IMMEDIATE — runs at execution time like CREATE, so a Forth-defined word that compiles a call to ' (e.g. `: SEE ' ... ;`) correctly consumes its *caller's* next input word when it executes, the same shared-cursor mechanism CREATE already relies on. Parses the next input word, looks it up, errors (`? unrecognized word`) if not found, else pushes its cfa. Added specifically because there was previously no way for Forth-level source to resolve a name to an xt at runtime — a real, necessary primitive addition, not a SEE-specific hack.

primitives.name: LATEST-ADDR
primitives.note: DEVELOPING.md §8 (VOCABULARY/USE): ( -- addr ) pushes the raw arena address of the LATEST sysvar cell itself (not its current value — LATEST already does that), so ordinary @/! can read and write it directly. Real Forth systems usually expose HERE/LATEST/STATE/BASE as ordinary variables rather than read-only accessors; this fixes that gap for LATEST specifically, the one VOCABULARY/USE need, rather than a blanket change.

primitives.name: EXECUTE
primitives.note: ( xt -- ) pops a code-field address and runs it exactly as if it had been called directly — DOCOL threading, DOVAR/DOCON/DODOES dispatch, breakpoints, and a blocking word (KEY/ACCEPT) inside it all behave identically to a normal call. Special-cased in inner.ts's dispatch(), never reaches primitives.ts's switch, because it needs to recurse into executeXT() itself (generator-level access a plain stack-effect primitive doesn't have), the same reason ACCEPT is handled there instead of here.

primitives.name: PAD
primitives.note: ( -- addr ) DEVELOPING.md §7, M16: pushes the base address of the PAD bank — the fixed, overwritten-on-next-use scratch region S" now copies interpreted-mode string text into. A free addition mirroring the HERE/LATEST precedent: PAD already needed to exist as a bank for S" to work, so exposing its address to Forth source costs nothing extra.

primitives.name: ABORT
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §9, M17: empties the data stack and throws a plain Error('ABORT'), surfacing via the same uncaught-error path every other error already uses (prints '? ABORT' at the top-level REPL). Deliberately NOT built on THROW/CATCH — that fuller exception model was scoped and then explicitly tabled ('probably not, unless a real need shows up'); this is the classic-Forth-useful subset of it that doesn't need any of that machinery.

primitives.name: BANK@
primitives.note: ( "tag" -- addr ) DEVELOPING.md §10/§12, M18/M20: parses the next input token (same nextInputToken() mechanism '/CREATE/VARIABLE/CONSTANT/S"/VOCABULARY/USE already use), uppercases it, looks up the first bank of that tag, pushes its base address, or throws '? unknown bank: <TAG>' on no match. addr only, matching the SOMETHING@ convention (fetch one value) — size deliberately not returned; a bank-inspection word can add it later if a real need shows up, not preemptively. M20: reads MMAP directly (ctx.banks.mmap.findBankAddr()) rather than calling BankTable.findBank() — a pure read-path swap, same observable behavior, since MMAP is a verified-correct mirror of the host array in the same creation order. Reaches shared and per-arena banks identically, no special-casing — multi-arena isolation is a confirmed non-goal (DEVELOPING.md §10), not something BANK@ needs to enforce. Combined with each sysvar group's known baseOffset (this file's sysvarGroups) and a field's own offset, 'BANK@ SYSV <offset> + @' reaches any sysvar from pure Forth source without a separate named-lookup primitive.

primitives.name: CREATE-BANK
primitives.note: ( size "tag" -- addr ) DEVELOPING.md §13, M21: pops size, parses the next input token, uppercases it, and calls ctx.banks.mmap.addBank(tag, tag, mmap.getNextFree(), size, RESIDENT|ACTIVE) directly — the exact same MemoryMap.addBank() method BankTable.createBank() already calls internally (M19), just invoked straight from a primitive instead of through the host, matching MMAP §11's original 'no host round-trip needed for creation' design. Name equals the (truncated) tag — no auto-serial scheme, no uniqueness check, since a primitive bypassing BankTable entirely has no business reaching BankTable's own private serial counter. No out-of-space check beyond MMAP's own 64-slot cap — relies on DataView's own bounds-checking at first real access, same precedent M19's BankTable constructor already relies on. Real, named consequence: a bank created this way is invisible to BankTable.getAllBanks()/findBank() and everything built on them (storage.ts, the app's read_banks WebMCP tool, the inspector panel) — only BANK@ (M20, reads MMAP directly) and raw MMAP reads see it. Not a gap, the direct structural cost of 'no host round-trip', named plainly in DEVELOPING.md §13 rather than glossed over.

primitives.name: XOR
primitives.note: ( a b -- a^b ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: same shape as AND(15)/OR(16) — a real bitwise op the M8 batch never shipped.

primitives.name: .S
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: non-destructive stack print, bottom-to-top, current BASE — reuses .'s (18) own digit-formatting loop applied to every cell (stack.ts's toArray() is top-to-bottom, reversed here to print deepest-first, matching classic Forth .S).

primitives.name: 2SWAP
primitives.note: ( a b c d -- c d a b ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: swaps the top two cell-pairs.

primitives.name: 2OVER
primitives.note: ( a b c d -- a b c d a b ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: copies the second-from-top pair to the top, generalizing OVER(4) the way 2DUP/2DROP(71/72) generalized DUP/DROP.

primitives.name: CELLS
primitives.note: ( n -- n*4 ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: n * CELL_SIZE.

primitives.name: CELL+
primitives.note: ( addr -- addr+4 ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: addr + CELL_SIZE.

primitives.name: FILL
primitives.note: ( addr len char -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: classic ANS signature — fills len bytes starting at addr with char's low 8 bits.

primitives.name: CMOVE
primitives.note: ( addr1 addr2 len -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: copies len bytes addr1->addr2, low-to-high. Like real Forth's CMOVE (not CMOVE>), an overlapping range where addr2 falls inside [addr1, addr1+len) corrupts data — a documented footgun, not a bug, same precedent as the >R/R>(37) imbalance note.

primitives.name: BL
primitives.note: ( -- 32 ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: pushes the ASCII space code — named as a candidate in CORE-VOCABULARY.md §12 itself.

primitives.name: SPACE
primitives.note: ( -- ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: BL EMIT as one word.

primitives.name: WITHIN
primitives.note: ( n lo hi -- flag ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: TRUE if lo <= n < hi. Deliberately plain signed, non-wraparound semantics, not full ANS WITHIN's modular-arithmetic definition — U<(92) already covers the one place unsigned comparison was actually needed, and no current caller needs wraparound ranges.

primitives.name: PICK
primitives.note: ( xu ... x1 x0 u -- xu ... x1 x0 xu ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: generalizes OVER (1 PICK = OVER, 0 PICK = DUP) to arbitrary depth.

primitives.name: ROLL
primitives.note: ( xu ... x1 x0 u -- xu-1 ... x1 x0 xu ) DEVELOPING.md §15, M23: generalizes ROT (2 ROLL = ROT) — pops u, then the item u cells down, shifting everything above it down by one and pushing the rolled item on top.

bankTags.DICT: dictionary / user program space, per-arena (in use since M2)
bankTags.RSTK: return stack, per-arena (in use since M2)
bankTags.CHAR: character-code grid, per-arena, 1 byte per cell, write-through into the framebuffer via ScreenHal (in use since M3, matches Rebel-ROM's CHAR bank exactly — docs/SCREEN-MODULE.md §3)
bankTags.SCRN: pixel framebuffer — NOT an arena bank in Rebel-Sim (matches Rebel-ROM: externally-backed, outside the arena's own memory accounting, excluded from the portable-dump claim per FORTH-ARCHITECTURE.md §8). Rebel-Sim's analog is the host-supplied ScreenHal implementation drawing to a <canvas>, never arena-resident memory.
bankTags.KMAP: raw-usage-code -> character translation table, u8[2][256] (unshifted/shifted planes), in use since M4 (docs/KEYBOARD.md §6). CLAUDE.md lists KMAP as shared/singular rather than per-arena like SCRN — Rebel-Sim only has one arena today (no multi-arena isolation yet), so it's allocated inside that arena like CHAR; the shared/singular distinction becomes visible once multi-arena support lands.
bankTags.TIB: Terminal Input Buffer, per-arena, in use since M7a — the resident scratch region ACCEPT reads a REPL line into. Not a Rebel-ROM-derived tag (no shipped Rebel-ROM Phase 11 yet, same status as Rebel-Sim-only DATA/FORTH group precedent) and not a persistable project-asset bank — Storage never touches it.
bankTags.PAD: Scratch text region, per-arena, in use since M16 (DEVELOPING.md §7) — holds the text S" copies in while interpreting, so its addr/len can be pushed and used immediately (e.g. by TYPE) without needing dictionary space. Rebel-Sim-only, no Rebel-ROM Phase 11 precedent yet, same status as TIB. Deliberately not reused for anything else (no reentrancy/nesting support) — overwritten unconditionally on each S" call, a documented footgun matching real Forth's own PAD semantics. Not a persistable project-asset bank — Storage never touches it.

CORE.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_CORE_OFFSET (0x010). Real TCoreSysVars also has SCREEN-MODE/COLOR-DEPTH/PALETTE-BANK/KEYMAP/LAST-ERROR — not implemented in Rebel-Sim yet, added when something needs them, same reserved-slot precedent as everywhere else in this table.

CURSOR-X.note: text cursor column. M3: owned by Screen, not bounds-checked on write (matches Rebel-ROM's SetCursor)

ARENA-SIZE.note: total arena size in bytes (Arena.sizeBytes), written once at Machine construction, read via getUnsigned/setUnsigned since it can exceed the signed 32-bit range (MAX_ARENA_SIZE is 4 GiB). The reverse of this group's usual direction: real TCoreSysVars doesn't have this field either (checked src/sysvars.h directly, not assumed) — CBankTable::GetArenaSize() is the equivalent C++-side fact, just not exposed as a sysvar there yet. A genuine cross-target candidate, not Rebel-Sim-only like the FORTH group's fields.

SCREEN.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_SCREEN_OFFSET (0x040) and screenmodule.h's TScreenSysVars. COLOR-DEPTH/PALETTE-SIZE omitted — Rebel-Sim's canvas HAL is truecolor-only, no palette-indirection mode to track.

CHAR-CELL-W.note: current glyph cell width in pixels

CHAR-CELL-H.note: current glyph cell height in pixels

CHAR-COLS.note: character grid width = SCREEN-WIDTH / CHAR-CELL-W; the actual addressing stride into the CHAR bank (docs/SCREEN-MODULE.md §3.2), not recomputed on the fly

INK.note: default foreground color (0xRRGGBB) for character writes

PAPER.note: default background color (0xRRGGBB) for character writes

KEYBOARD.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_KEYBOARD_OFFSET (0x080). M4: populated with MODIFIERS only — real TKeyboardSysVars also has nKeyboardCount (attached-device count), omitted here since browser DOM APIs have no USB-hotplug-style device enumeration to report; there's always implicitly 'some keyboard'.

MODIFIERS.note: live modifier bitmask (docs/KEYBOARD.md §2): bit0-3 = L Ctrl/Shift/Alt/GUI, bit4-7 = R Ctrl/Shift/Alt/GUI. Updated on every modifier press/release pseudo-event (0x80+bit convention).

FONT.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_FONT_OFFSET (0x0C0), Rebel-ROM's Phase 6 font-blob system. Rebel-Sim doesn't have a Forth-addressable FONT bank — M3's glyph bitmap is a static host-side asset in packages/app, not arena memory — so this group stays reserved/empty rather than reimplemented.

STORAGE.note: matches src/sysvars.h's SYSVARS_STORAGE_OFFSET (0x140). Reserved, populated when M5 lands.

FORTH.note: Rebel-Sim-only group (Rebel-ROM's Phase 11/Forth doesn't exist yet) — appended after Rebel-ROM's real groups (STORAGE ends at 0x180) rather than colliding with them, same 64-byte-slot incremental-reservation pattern.

SP0.note: data stack base address (reserved, M1-M3 hardcode the DSTK bank size instead)

LATEST.note: most recently defined dictionary entry's address, 0 = empty dictionary (in use since M2)
